summary: Compound: a sustained, specifically-shaped partial Postgres outage (result_sets table unreachable via lock/exhaustion, execution_tracker.executions writable-except-cancel) makes the new quota_check_degraded refusal's own mark_cancelled cleanup ALSO fail (same degraded pool), leaving an orphaned running execution row (agents_targeted=0) per retry cycle. Chaos-injector (CH-1) derived MEDIUM not HIGH/P0 (no reaper/cap consumes these rows, so it's audit/drawer clutter during the outage, not a persistent post-recovery DoS). sre further recalibrated: execution_tracker.executions has NO reaper for ANY row status today (pre-existing gap, not new), so the marginal orphan count is a rounding error against that baseline; recovery is NOT automatic -- a manual per-row POST /api/executions/:id/cancel is needed once Postgres recovers. create_execution does not itself publish to the SSE ExecutionEventBus (only later state-transition methods do), so an orphan is not immediately pushed to a live dashboard drawer, but WOULD surface on any list/poll of executions that displays running rows.
trigger: a sustained partial Postgres degradation (result_sets unreachable, executions writable-except-cancel) combined with a caller retrying per the new retry_after_ms=5000 hint

summary: No dedicated Prometheus metric for the new degraded-read refusal classes (quota_check_degraded, store_degraded reason strings are audit-log/free-text only). ResultSetStore has zero MetricsRegistry wiring, unlike 6+ sibling stores (InstructionStore, RuntimeConfigStore, UpdateRegistry, SessionStore, CommandOutboxStore, GatewayRouteStore, OfflineEndpointStore) that carry the documented <store>_read_degrade_total{reason} convention (docs/observability-conventions.md lines 62-78). yuzu_result_set_quota_rejected fires only for the authoritative post-dispatch QuotaExceeded outcome, never for any of the 4 new _checked DbError fail-closed refusals. Capped at MEDIUM not HIGH: a sustained/fleet-wide degradation of this shape trips the existing YuzuPgPoolSaturated/YuzuPgAcquireWaitHigh alerts (both stores share the one PgPool), so the systemic case has a redundant signal; a scoped result-set-only degradation is genuinely invisible. Independently confirmed by compliance-officer (same Gate 6 wave, CC7.2 angle) without having seen this report.
trigger: a Postgres degradation scoped narrowly enough to affect only ResultSetStore's reads, not the shared pool broadly

summary: MCP's 3 async producers emit kInternalError with the literal prefix 'RESULT_SET_STORE_UNAVAILABLE:' on BOTH the pre-dispatch quota-check failure (safe to retry) and the post-dispatch create_pending DbError (never retry) -- same JSON-RPC error code both times, discriminable only by retry_after_ms (5000 vs null).
